title: RMP vs TSG
summary: Warrior dies: eight answers, none of them magic-immune. Cyclone on your Priest is what beats you — he has no kick and no escape.

sections.title: Warrior dies, not the Death Knight
sections.body: Counts: Warrior 8, DK 7, Druid 5. The Druid is thinnest but is the hardest to hold. The DK's seven are the misleading ones — Anti-Magic Shell (40s), Anti-Magic Zone and Lichborne blank most of what a Mage and a Priest do, so half his kit is built for you. The Warrior's eight are generic. Rallying Cry is party-wide — it blunts the whole attempt rather than saving him, so price it against the go.

sections.title: Opener — nothing is cast from nothing

steps.note: On the Druid. No cooldown, so the go starts before it costs anything.
Re-CC the Druid as Sap breaks. Same DR, so it is the short one.
Opens on the Warrior the global the Poly lands.
On the Mage. 2 min — only in every second go.

sections.title: The go — Kidney is the window, not the opener

steps.note: 90s. This is the term the cadence is built on.
Fresh stun DR after Cheap Shot, so half duration. Accept it.
Lands inside the Kidney, not before it.
Only if he still holds Die by the Sword — it is a parry buff.

sections.title: What the Warrior answers with — all eight

steps.note: 30% all damage for 8s. Back every second go.
25s, so up every go. Do not open a cast into it.
Party-wide. Blunts the go, does not save him.
Breaks fear and blocks it for 6s. Not a damage answer.
No cooldown. Your Priest has no kick and no escape.
30s ranged stun. It arrives every cadence.
45s silence. Kills the Pain Suppression, not the heal.

sections.title: Where this is guessing
sections.body: The plan assumes your Rogue can hold the Warrior, who has Charge on 17s and Heroic Leap on 30s. If he cannot, you have chosen a target you cannot pin and the DK's magic immunities make the swap worse than the original. That trade is not resolved here.
